0:05 Now we come to another question. What is the modern
era? Where do we start?
And why do we start where we start? It is very common
0:13
and customary in the writing of Middle Eastern history
to start the modern era in 1798. Why 1798?
Because in 1798 Napoleon invaded Egypt, and ushered
0:28
in through his invasion, a long period of rapid and
radical change. That sounds reasonable. But it is
problematic.
0:47
Because in this determination of the Napoleonic
invasion as the beginning of the modern era, there is a
hidden assumption. That hidden assumption is, that
the modern era in the Middle East was created only and
solely through European influence and European
supremacy on an area which is in decline, stagnant and
moving nowhere. So there is now a historiographical
debate about whether it was ever really correct to begin
the modern era with the Napoleonic invasion of Egypt.
